build.title: Build a cohort you can defend
build.blurb: Four things that keep your counts honest.

steps.title: It asks before it guesses
steps.body: If a request could mean two things, you choose, seeing how many samples each answer keeps.
steps.narration: If your request could mean two different things, Cohort Studio asks first. Every answer shows how many samples it would keep, so you choose with the numbers in front of you.

steps.title: Double counts, caught
steps.body: Every step shows its count. A join that counts a sample twice is flagged, and fixed in one click.
steps.narration: Every step shows exactly how many samples are left. When a join starts counting the same sample twice, it's flagged in pink. One click on Fix it, and every sample counts once again.

steps.title: A verdict with evidence
steps.body: Each cohort is rated Ready, Conditional or Blocked, with every check behind it.
steps.narration: Each cohort gets an honest verdict: ready, conditional, or blocked. Open it to see every check behind it, and what a person still needs to review.

find.label: At the top of every result

steps.title: Take it anywhere
steps.body: Download the sample list and a script that rebuilds it exactly, or open it on the canvas.
steps.narration: When it's ready, download the sample list, and a Python script that rebuilds the cohort exactly. Or open it on the canvas, and keep shaping it visually.

canvas.title: Meet the canvas
canvas.blurb: Build cohorts visually, with honest counts on every card.

steps.title: Your cohort as a pipeline
steps.body: Each card is one step with the engine's own count. Wires are drawn to scale.
steps.narration: This is your cohort as a pipeline. Every card is one step, with the real count from the engine. And every wire is drawn to scale, so you can see where samples drop away.

steps.title: See why, then fix it
steps.body: A join that adds rows turns pink. X-ray a real patient to see why, then fix it in one click.
steps.narration: A join that adds extra rows turns pink. Tap See why to X-ray a real patient, and watch their slides become rows. Then one click on Fix, and every sample counts once.

find.label: The pink pill under a join

steps.title: Drop in any step
steps.body: Press Add, then drag a block onto any wire. Any join it needs is added for you.
steps.narration: Press Add to open the blocks. Drag one onto any wire, and it slots right in. If it needs data from another table, the join is added for you.

steps.title: See what a row means
steps.body: Grain lanes place each card by what one row stands for. A double-counting join drops a lane.
steps.narration: Switch on grain lanes to see what one row stands for: a patient, a sample, or several rows per sample. A join that double counts drops a lane, and its fix brings it back.

steps.title: Code you can check
steps.body: Open Code for SQL, Python or the raw steps. The SQL is run and checked against the engine.
steps.narration: Open Code to see the same cohort as SQL, Python, or the raw steps. The SQL isn't just written. It's run, and checked against the engine, step by step.
steps.say: Open Code to see the same cohort as S.Q.L., Python, or the raw steps. The S.Q.L. isn't just written. It's run, and checked against the engine, step by step.

compare.title: Compare two cohorts
compare.blurb: Who they share, and how they differ.

steps.title: Any two cohorts
steps.body: Pick saved cohorts, favourites or two versions of one. Both rerun on the same frozen data.
steps.narration: Pick any two cohorts: saved ones, favourites, or two versions of the same cohort. Both are rerun on the same frozen data, so the comparison is fair.

find.label: The two slots at the top

steps.title: Who they share
steps.body: The overlap drawn to scale, and plain sentences on what the numbers say.
steps.narration: See exactly who the two cohorts share, drawn to scale, with plain sentences that say what the numbers mean.

steps.title: How they differ
steps.body: Who is in each, the data each has, and survival curves with one record per patient.
steps.narration: Then see how they differ: who is in each, which data they have, and survival curves, with one record per patient.

practice.title: Learn by doing
practice.blurb: Five short tasks. Each one ticks itself off when you do it.

tasks.title: Answer a clarifying question
tasks.hint: Ask for HR+ / HER2− tumours and pick a definition.
tasks.coach: Pick one of the answers: each shows how many samples it keeps.

tasks.title: Fix a double count
tasks.hint: Load the double-count demo and press Fix.
tasks.coach: Press Fix on the pink pill under the join.

tasks.title: Drag a block onto a wire
tasks.hint: Press Add, then drop a block between two cards.
tasks.coach: Drag ER status from the blocks onto a number on a wire.

tasks.title: Check the SQL is verified
tasks.hint: Open Code and look for the Verified badge.
tasks.coach: The Code panel is open: look for the Verified badge above the SQL.

tasks.title: Compare two cohorts
tasks.hint: Save two cohorts, then pick both on Compare.
tasks.coach: Pick a cohort for A and another for B at the top.
